mainTopic: Whether a caesarean-born (יוצא דופן) animal can become קדשים, and a ברייתא on a woman who gives birth by caesarean after three days of labor.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא where רבי שמעון explains which disqualified offerings stay on the מזבח: those whose פסול happened בקודש stay, and the others come down. The גמרא uses this ברייתא as a proof that an animal born יוצא דופן cannot become valid קדשים, which supports רבי יוחנן. רב הונא בריה דרב נתן suggests the ברייתא might mean a בכור instead. The back-and-forth that follows shows that the קדשים reading makes better sense. A verse ('אמו' 'אמו') already teaches about a חולין animal consecrated after birth, so the ברייתא's verse is needed for the offspring of a holy animal. With a בכור, by contrast, 'פטר רחם' already covers everything. The גמרא supports this from the other animals on the ברייתא's list, which are already excluded elsewhere, so two verses must exist there too: one for חולין and one for קדשים. The גמרא then turns to a new ברייתא about a woman in hard labor for three days whose baby is born by caesarean. There the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון disagree about her status as a זבה and about blood that comes out 'from there'. רבינא begins to define the case of the second disagreement, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבי שמעון's rule: which disqualified offerings stay on the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון concludes that the verse includes offerings whose פסול happened in the קודש, and excludes those whose פסול did not happen in the קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the verse both included and excluded, you should say: I include those whose disqualification happened in the holy place, and I exclude those whose disqualification did not happen in the holy place.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a ברייתא that the גמרא has been quoting. רבי שמעון gives the rule for which disqualified offerings stay on the מזבח and which must be taken down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse has a word that includes (a ריבוי) and a word that excludes (a מיעוט). רבי שמעון splits the cases: if the problem arose in the קודש, during the service, the offering stays on the מזבח. If the problem existed before the service began, it comes down. The list in this ברייתא includes יוצא דופן among the ones that come down, and the next step builds on that.

keyTerms.meaning: included; the verse adds cases
excluded; the verse limits cases
their disqualification
in the holy place, during the Temple service

phrases.english: After the verse included and excluded, you should say:
I include those
phrases.notes: He means those that stay on the מזבח and are not taken down.

phrases.english: whose disqualification was in the holy place,
and I exclude those
whose disqualification was not in the holy place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that the earlier part of the daf began quoting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings disqualified in the קודש stay on the מזבח; offerings disqualified before the service come down.

steps.title: Proof that a caesarean-born animal cannot be an offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists יוצא דופן among the cases that come down from the מזבח. The גמרא suggests this means a regular animal of קדשים, which would support רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it teaches that a caesarean-born animal does not stay. Isn't that talking about a caesarean-born animal of קדשים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא as evidence. רבי שמעון counts a יוצא דופן animal as unfit, so it must come down from the מזבח, and the גמרא reads this as talking about ordinary קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though רבי שמעון holds that a human caesarean birth counts as a real birth, this ברייתא would show that he agrees an animal born this way cannot become a valid offering. That supports רבי יוחנן's position.

keyTerms.meaning: born through the side; a caesarean birth
in any case, it teaches
is it not...? (the opening of a suggested proof)
consecrated animals, offerings

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches that a caesarean-born animal does not [stay],
Is it not talking about a caesarean-born animal of consecrated offerings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just quoted as evidence.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that a יוצא דופן animal cannot become valid קדשים, and that רבי שמעון agrees about animals.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון listing יוצא דופן among the offerings that come down from the מזבח.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא means a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן rejects the proof: the ברייתא may be talking about a בכור born by caesarean.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב נתן said: No, it means a caesarean-born firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא pushes back on the proof. He says the ברייתא could be about a בכור born יוצא דופן, so it tells us nothing about ordinary קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא only means a בכור, then it says nothing about whether someone can consecrate a caesarean-born animal as a regular קרבן. That removes the support for רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: a firstborn animal, holy from birth

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan said:
No, it means a caesarean-born firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 2 by reading the ברייתא as talking about a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא, not רבי יוחנן's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא means ordinary קדשים, but it could mean a בכור.

steps.title: A caesarean firstborn is not holy at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a caesarean בכור is already excluded by 'פטר רחם', so it is plainly not holy, and the ברייתא would have no reason to teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A firstborn? That is learned from 'opens the womb'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's reading. A בכור born by caesarean has no holiness at all, since the תורה says a בכור is one that 'opens the womb'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal is not holy at all, then it is just a regular animal. Of course it comes down from the מזבח. So why would רבי שמעון need to list it in the ברייתא?

keyTerms.meaning: 'opens the womb'; the תורה's wording for a בכור
it is derived (from a verse)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the בכור is holy. Everyone agrees it is not. The question is why the ברייתא would bother to mention something so obvious.

phrases.english: A firstborn? That is learned from 'opens the womb'!
phrases.notes: שמות 13:2. Only an animal that comes out of the womb is a holy בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading proposed in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן's reading that the ברייתא means a caesarean בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A caesarean בכור is not holy at all because of 'פטר רחם', so it is obvious that it comes down from the מזבח. The ברייתא would not need to teach it.

steps.title: The same problem hits the other reading too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ordinary קדשים born by caesarean are also excluded by a verse ('אמו' 'אמו'). So the objection works against either reading and is no reason to prefer the קדשים reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what would you say, that it means קדשים? That is also learned from 'its mother', 'its mother'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by throwing the question back. The קדשים reading has the exact same problem, so the objection does not help the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה from the word 'אמו' teaches that a caesarean animal cannot become קדשים at all. That would make it plainly non-holy, and obviously it would come down from the מזבח. Since both readings make the ברייתא's statement look obvious, the objection cannot be used to reject רב הונא's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, what (would you say)?
'its mother'; a word used for a גזירה שוה between בכור and קדשים
a teaching drawn from the same word appearing in two places

steps.whatToRemember: Whether the ברייתא means a בכור or ordinary קדשים, a caesarean-born animal is not holy at all, each from its own verse. The question 'why would the ברייתא need to say this?' therefore hits both readings equally.

phrases.english: Rather, what would you say, that it means consecrated offerings?
That too is learned from 'its mother', 'its mother'!
phrases.notes: This is the link רבי יוחנן made earlier: 'אמו' appears for a בכור and also for קדשים (ויקרא 22:27).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 4 by showing it applies just as much to the reading in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-question: shows the difficulty applies equally to the alternative reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The objection seemed to rule out the בכור reading and leave the קדשים reading standing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ordinary קדשים born by caesarean are also excluded by a verse, so the objection does not favor either reading.

steps.title: The two readings are not equal: only the קדשים reading needs a second verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer from Step 5. With ordinary קדשים there are two different cases, so two verses make sense. With a בכור, 'פטר רחם' already covers it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of comparison is this? If the ברייתא is talking about קדשים, we understand why two verses are needed. One verse is for a חולין animal born by caesarean that was consecrated later. The other is for the caesarean offspring of a קדשים animal, which is holy from birth. But if the ברייתא is talking about a בכור, that case is already learned from 'פטר רחם'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. It shows that the קדשים reading leaves a real job for the ברייתא's verse, while the בכור reading leaves its verse with nothing to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 claimed that both readings face the same problem, because a verse already excludes both cases. The גמרא now shows they are not the same. With קדשים, the 'אמו אמו' link covers only a חולין animal consecrated after birth. The caesarean offspring of a holy mother is holy from birth and still needs the ברייתא's own verse. With a בכור, one verse ('פטר רחם') covers everything, so the ברייתא's verse would be pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is this?' The גמרא rejects a comparison as not equal.
'Granted / it makes sense': one side works well, but the other does not.
Through the side, meaning a caesarean birth.
The offspring of holy animals are holy from the moment they come into being.

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different caesarean cases here. One is a חולין animal born by caesarean and consecrated later. The other is the offspring of an animal that was already קדשים. Only the second is holy from birth, and that is why it needs its own verse.

phrases.english: What is this [comparison]?
Granted, if you say [the ברייתא is about] קדשים,
that is why two verses were needed:
one for a non-holy animal
that was born by caesarean, and then he consecrated it,
and one for a holy animal
that gave birth by caesarean,
and he holds that the offspring of קדשים
are holy from the moment they come into being.
But if you say [it is about] a בכור,
that is already learned from "opens the womb"!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי? אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּקָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 5's claim that the problem weighs equally on both readings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 5, which treated the בכור reading and the קדשים reading as equally problematic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With קדשים there are two separate cases (consecrated after birth versus holy from birth), so two verses are justified. With a בכור, one verse covers it fully, so the ברייתא's verse would be wasted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This brings back the proof for רבי יוחנן from Step 2: the ברייתא is best read as talking about ordinary קדשים.

steps.title: Support from the other animals on the ברייתא's list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that the קדשים reading is also reasonable. The proof comes from the other cases the ברייתא lists.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense to read it this way, because the ברייתא lists: an animal that mated with a person, an animal used for bestiality, an animal set aside for idolatry, an animal that was worshipped, and a mixed breed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings extra support for the קדשים reading by pointing to the ברייתא's list. It is setting up the next step, which explains why this list helps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is proven yet. The גמרא only names the other cases on the ברייתא's list. The next step shows what is special about these cases and why they point toward the קדשים reading.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So too it makes sense': the גמרא adds support for a conclusion.
An animal that mated with a person.
An animal that a person used for bestiality.
An animal set aside to be offered to an idol.
An animal that was itself worshipped as an idol.
A mixed breed born from two different species.

phrases.english: So too it makes sense [this way],
since it teaches:
"the animal that mated with a person, and the animal used for bestiality,
and the one set aside [for idolatry], and the one worshipped, and the mixed breed."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds extra support for the conclusion of Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the ברייתא's יוצא דופן is ordinary קדשים (supporting רבי יוחנן).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The other cases the ברייתא lists as coming down from the מזבח.

steps.title: These animals are already excluded by a different verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רובע, נרבע, נעבד and מוקצה are already excluded by ויקרא 1:2. So why does the ברייתא need its own verse for them?
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these learned from here? They are learned from somewhere else! 'From the animal' excludes the רובע and the נרבע. 'From the herd' excludes the נעבד. 'From the flock' excludes the מוקצה. 'And from the flock' excludes the animal that gored.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the proof from step 7. These animals are already excluded from being offerings by a different verse, so the ברייתא's verse must be teaching something else about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויקרא 1:2 already shows that an ordinary animal with these problems can never be made holy. Yet the ברייתא lists them again as coming down from the מזבח. So the ברייתא must mean a different case: an animal that was already קדשים when it had this problem. Step 10 draws the conclusion for יוצא דופן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Are these learned from here? They are learned from there!': a source for this law already exists elsewhere.
'To exclude': this word in the verse rules out a certain case.
An animal that gored and killed a person.

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the ברייתא's verse is not wasted. It teaches that even an animal that is already קדשים must come down from the מזבח if it has one of these problems, because its פסול did not happen בקודש (in the Temple service), as רבי שמעון said in step 1.

phrases.english: Are these learned from here?
They are learned from there!
"From the animal"
comes to exclude the one that mated with a person and the one used for bestiality;
"from the herd" comes to exclude the one that was worshipped;
"from the flock" comes to exclude the one set aside [for idolatry];
"and from the flock" comes to exclude the one that gored.
phrases.notes: The extra 'and' (the letter ו) is what teaches this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof of step 7 by showing that these cases already have a different source for ordinary animals.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the ברייתא's verse is the source that excludes רובע, נרבע, נעבד and מוקצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These animals are already excluded by ויקרא 1:2 before they are ever made holy, so the ברייתא's verse would be needed only for a case where they were already holy when they became disqualified.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the ברייתא's verse (and its יוצא דופן) is about animals that are already קדשים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 1:2 ('מן הבהמה', 'מן הבקר', 'מן הצאן', 'ומן הצאן') already excludes these animals when they are ordinary.

steps.title: Mixed breeds and look-alikes are already excluded by a different verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second piece to its proof. An animal of כלאים and a נדמה are already excluded from being offerings by ויקרא 22:27, so the ברייתא's verse must be teaching something else about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more: do we really learn about a mixed-breed animal from here? We learn it from another place: 'a bull or a sheep or a goat.' 'Bull' leaves out a mixed breed, and 'or a goat' leaves out a look-alike!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the proof from step 8. It points to two more items in the ברייתא's list that already have their own source somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed that רובע, נרבע, נעבד and מוקצה are already excluded by ויקרא 1:2. Now the גמרא shows the same problem for כלאים and נדמה, which come from ויקרא 22:27. So the extra verse in the ברייתא looks unneeded for these cases too.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore. It adds another difficulty to the one already raised.
An animal born from two different species mixed together.
A look-alike: an animal that looks like a different species from its mother.
It is learned from there, meaning from a different verse.

phrases.english: And furthermore, is the law of a mixed-breed animal learned from here?
It is learned from there:
"A bull or a sheep or a goat"
"Bull" leaves out a mixed breed,
"Or a goat" leaves out a look-alike!
phrases.notes: A look-alike is something like a lamb born to a sheep that looks like a goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel difficulty to the one raised in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of a separate verse to exclude כלאים and נדמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse is not needed for something another verse already teaches, and ויקרא 22:27 already excludes כלאים and נדמה.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the ברייתא's verse is about animals that are already קדשים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 22:27 ('שור או כשב או עז') already excludes כלאים and נדמה.

steps.title: Two verses are needed: one for ordinary animals, one for sacrificial animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that each case needs two verses. One teaches that an ordinary animal of this kind cannot become an offering. The other teaches about an animal that is already holy. The same is true for a caesarean birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, two verses are needed: one for an ordinary animal, and one for a sacrificial animal. Here too, two verses are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the proof it began in Step 7. Since these disqualified animals already have a source elsewhere, the ברייתא's verse must be teaching about animals that are already holy. The same is true for the caesarean case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One verse teaches that a disqualified בהמת חולין cannot be made holy. The second verse teaches about a בהמת קדשים that is already holy: it may not be offered, and if it was put on the מזבח by mistake it must be taken down. Since this is true for the other cases in the list, the caesarean case can also have two verses. That supports the קדשים reading of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses are needed.
An ordinary animal that is not holy.
An animal that is already holy, for example because its mother was a holy animal.
Here too. It applies the same idea to the case being discussed.

steps.whatToRemember: Two verses can teach two different things about the same kind of disqualified animal: one for חולין and one for קדשים. So the caesarean case also fits the קדשים reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the support for reading the ברייתא as talking about קדשים, and so supports רבי יוחנן's view that a caesarean-born animal cannot become a valid offering.

phrases.english: Rather, two verses are needed:
one for an ordinary, non-holy animal,
and one for a sacrificial animal.
Here too, two verses are needed.
phrases.notes: "Here" means the animal born by caesarean, the case the ברייתא was teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the proof begun in step 7 and continued in steps 8 and 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two verses: one for חולין and one for קדשים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since another verse already excludes these animals, the ברייתא's verse seemed unneeded.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both verses are needed, one for חולין and one for קדשים, and the same applies to a caesarean birth.

steps.title: A woman in hard labor for three days whose baby is born by caesarean
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: if a woman was in hard labor for three days and the baby then came out by caesarean, the תנא קמא says she counts as giving birth while a זבה, and רבי שמעון says she does not. Blood that comes out from there is impure according to the תנא קמא, and רבי שמעון says it is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a woman who was in hard labor for three days, and the baby came out through the side wall, counts as one who gave birth as a זבה. רבי שמעון says: she does not count as one who gave birth as a זבה. Blood that comes out from there is impure, and רבי שמעון says it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא with two disagreements between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון about a caesarean birth after three days of labor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bleeding during the days of labor does not make a woman a זבה if a real birth follows, because the bleeding is blamed on the birth. The תנא קמא holds that a caesarean is not a real birth for this law, so her bleeding stays זיבה. רבי שמעון holds that a caesarean does count as a birth, so she is not a זבה. They also disagree about blood that comes out "from there."

keyTerms.meaning: A woman having a hard, painful labor.
Through the side wall of the body, meaning a caesarean birth.
A woman who gives birth while she has the status of a זבה.
Declares it pure.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two disagreements. The first is about the woman's status as a זבה. The second is only about whether certain blood is impure.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A woman who is in hard labor for three days,
and the baby came out through the side wall,
she counts as one who gave birth as a זבה,
And Rabbi Shimon says:
she does not count as one who gave birth as a זבה,
And blood that comes out from there is impure,
and Rabbi Shimon says it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section about a caesarean birth and the laws of זבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says a woman who gives birth by caesarean after three days of labor counts as giving birth as a זבה, and blood from there is impure. רבי שמעון disagrees on both points.

steps.title: What is the second disagreement in the ברייתא about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the first disagreement is easy to understand, because each side follows its known view about a caesarean birth. But it asks what the second disagreement, about the blood, is about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part is fine: רבי שמעון follows his own reasoning and the רבנן follow theirs. But the last part, what are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא, and this sets up רבינא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, each side follows its known view about whether a caesarean counts as a birth, as in the משנה. In the סיפא, it is not clear what the case is, so we cannot tell what the argument is about. The גמרא wants the exact case defined.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense. This sets up a contrast with a part that is unclear.
The first part of a teaching.
The last part of a teaching.
Following his own line of reasoning.

phrases.english: Granted, the first part is clear:
Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning,
phrases.notes: In the משנה, רבי שמעון holds that a caesarean birth counts as a birth.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis follow their own reasoning,
but the last part, what are they arguing about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the ברייתא quoted in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exact case the סיפא is describing, and what רבי שמעון and the רבנן are arguing about in it.

steps.title: רבינא begins to define the case in the second part
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the סיפא is talking about a case where the baby came out by caesarean. His explanation continues after this line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: for example, where the baby came out through the side wall.
